items.stem: A national backbone needs scalable IGP hierarchy. Which IS-IS design supports this best?

options.text: A level-1/level-2 hierarchy with regional L1 areas
options.rationale: Correct: L1/L2 hierarchy scales by summarising regional areas into the L2 core.

options.text: A single flat level-2 domain for all routers
options.rationale: A flat domain does not scale to a national backbone.

options.text: Running OSPF and IS-IS on every link simultaneously
options.rationale: Running both IGPs everywhere adds complexity without scaling benefit.
Static routing cannot scale or converge for a backbone.

items.explanation: Correct: L1/L2 hierarchy scales by summarising regional areas into the L2 core.

items.stem: Which statement about Segment Routing with MPLS is correct?

options.text: The path is encoded in the packet header, removing per-flow core state
options.rationale: Correct: SR source-routes via a label stack, so the core holds no per-flow state.

options.text: Every core router must hold per-flow RSVP state
options.rationale: That describes RSVP-TE, not Segment Routing.

options.text: It requires LDP on every node to function
options.rationale: SR-MPLS does not require LDP; it distributes labels via the IGP.
SR explicitly supports traffic engineering via segment lists.

items.explanation: Correct: SR source-routes via a label stack, so the core holds no per-flow state.

items.stem: Which TWO identifiers are required to deliver an MPLS L3VPN correctly for multiple customers? (Select TWO)

options.text: Route distinguisher (RD) to keep prefixes unique
options.rationale: Correct: the RD makes overlapping customer prefixes unique in VPNv4.
Correct: RTs control which VRFs import and export the routes.

options.text: A shared public IP for all customers
options.rationale: A shared public IP does not separate customer routing.
